answer: Forced-Divergence Task Lottery: each identity must submit a distinct work artifact whose history is keyed to a random seed, so an operator running many clones must either let them diverge (breaking the clone equivalence that made mass registration cheap) or absorb the cost of maintaining separate state per identity. Divergence is enforced by cross-checking artifact lineage at a karst-like fork point where any shared ancestry flags duplicates. An attacker cloning N agents pays N times the compute and storage to forge independent histories at the wharf of registration,
